text: BOOK VI, CHAPTER 1: THE SAPTANGA THEORY OF THE SEVEN LIMBS OF STATE According to the Saptanga theory expounded in this compendium, a sovereign state is constituted by seven interdependent organic limbs (Prakritis): 1. Swamin (The Sovereign Ruler or King) 2. Amatya (The Council of Ministers and High Officials) 3. Janapada (The Territory and its Settled Population) 4. Durga (The Fortified Capital and Defensive Strongholds) 5. Kosha (The Royal Treasury and Financial Reserves) 6. Danda or Bala (The Standing Army and Coercive Authority) 7. Mitra (The Steadfast Foreign Ally)

text: BOOK I, CHAPTER 16: CLASSIFICATION AND AUTHORITY OF ENVOYS (DUTAS) In diplomatic missions, envoys (Dutas) are classified into exactly three distinct categories based on their level of authority: 1. Nisrishtarthah: A Plenipotentiary Ambassador endowed with full ministerial qualifications and discretionary authority to negotiate treaties. 2. Parimitarthah: An Envoy Extraordinary entrusted with a strictly limited, predefined mission. 3. Shasanaharah: A Royal Messenger or Bearer of Dispatches authorized only to deliver written decrees.
